newsitem.title: UK: Harvey Nichols reports increased annual profits.
newsitem.headline: Harvey Nichols reports increased annual profits.

text.p: Harvey Nichols Group, the London department store, said on Monday it increased annual profits and current sales were ahead of last year.
The store, which is owned by multimillionaire Hong Kong businessman Dickson Poon, lifted pretax profit for the year to March 29, 1997 to 12.1 million pounds ($20 million) from 9.2 million last time.

Sector analysts had been looking for profits to jump to around 13 million pounds and shares in the company had fallen 7-1/2 pence to 294 pence shortly after the results announcement. The store said that cumulative sales for the first ten weeks of the current financial year are up 15 percent on the same period last year.

The group will be paying a final dividend of 3.9 pence per share making a total for the year of 5.8 pence per share. Poon bought the store for 51 million pounds in October 1991 and floated off 49.9 percent of it just five years later, raising 150 million pounds. Poon is also head of Hong Kong based Dickson Concepts.
